 Judgment
1.
These appeals are filed by the claimants as well as by the insurer.
2.  The insurer contends that admittedly three people were being carried in a motor cycle when the accident occurred.

It also contends that it is not in dispute that the chargesheet was laid against the rider of the motorcycle and notwithstanding these glaring facts, the Tribunal has held that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent only to the extent of 50%.
3. It is the case of the insurer that the entire negligence had to be attributed on the rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the car ought to have been exonerated of all liability.

4. Learned counsel for the claimants, on the other hand, contends that the Tribunal was justified in coming to the conclusion that both the rider of the motorcycle as well as the driver of the car had contributed to the accident.
She submits that there is absolutely no evidence indicating that the accident occurred due to any negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle.

She also contends that merely three people were riding in the motorcycle cannot by itself lead to inference that there is Sri Mahendra Prasad B C vs The Manager on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21555954/
7 negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

sentences.text: She contends that the attribution of 50% on the rider of the motorcycle itself was incorrect, given the fact that the driver of the car was not examined.
5. It is not in dispute that on the complaint lodged by the driver of the car, a chargesheet had been lodged against the rider of the motorcycle.
It is also not in dispute that on the complaint filed by rider of the motorcycle alleging negligence on the driver of the car a 'B' report has been filed.

6. Be that as it may, in order to establish that there was negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle,
- 10 - the driver of the car ought to have been examined.

However, the driver of the car has chosen to stay away from the Tribunal and as a consequence, the best possible evidence was unavailable to the Tribunal to ascertain as to who was responsible for the accident.

The evidence on record also indicates that the accident occurred at a time when the cauvery riots were taking place and given this background, the Tribunal, in my view, was justified in holding that both the owner of the car and rider of the motorcycle had contributed equally to the accident.
7.
The apportionment of negligence, therefore, to the extent of 50:50 cannot be found fault with.
As far as compensation is concerned, though no Doctor was examined, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation after deducting 50% towards negligence.
8. In my view, this assessment of compensation by the Tribunal on the basis of the evidence available on record cannot be found fault with.
Consequently, both the - 11 - appeals of the insurer and the appeals of the claimants are dismissed.
9. However, it is noticed that interest at 7% per annum is ordered.
In my view, it would be appropriate to award interest, as has been normally done, at 6% per annum in respect of the compensation.
10. The amount in deposit, if any, is directed to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.

opennyai_summary.facts:
2.  The insurer contends that admittedly three people were being carried in a motor cycle when the accident occurred.
It also contends that it is not in dispute that the chargesheet was laid against the rider of the motorcycle and notwithstanding these glaring facts, the Tribunal has held that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent only to the extent of 50%.
opennyai_summary.issue: 3. It is the case of the insurer that the entire negligence had to be attributed on the rider of the motorcycle and the driver of the car ought to have been exonerated of all liability.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
4. Learned counsel for the claimants, on the other hand, contends that the Tribunal was justified in coming to the conclusion that both the rider of the motorcycle as well as the driver of the car had contributed to the accident.
She also contends that merely three people were riding in the motorcycle cannot by itself lead to inference that there is Sri Mahendra Prasad B C vs The Manager on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21555954/
7 negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.
She contends that the attribution of 50% on the rider of the motorcycle itself was incorrect, given the fact that the driver of the car was not examined.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, the driver of the car has chosen to stay away from the Tribunal and as a consequence, the best possible evidence was unavailable to the Tribunal to ascertain as to who was responsible for the accident.
The apportionment of negligence, therefore, to the extent of 50:50 cannot be found fault with.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Consequently, both the - 11 - appeals of the insurer and the appeals of the claimants are dismissed.
9. However, it is noticed that interest at 7% per annum is ordered.
In my view, it would be appropriate to award interest, as has been normally done, at 6% per annum in respect of the compensation.
10. The amount in deposit, if any, is directed to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
